newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed lower on Monday with the market lacking impetus from the U.S. and London with those markets closed due to bank holidays.
Dealers said most business was done in the 2001 to 2006 area and there was already some business in the grey market for the Dutch 10-year bond which will be reopened tomorrow.
The Dutch state said last week it would reopen the 5.75 percent February 2007 with sales starting on Tuesday.
"If this bond is taken in well, this would be a good sign for the market as business has been directionless recently," said one dealer.
The February 2007 bond closed 0.24 lower at 99.48/58 and dealers said the second tranche was priced at 99.30/35 in the grey market in late afternoon trade.
The bund futures contract was lingering at 100.70, down 0.25 late today and this was seen as an important support level.
"If the June futures contract drops below this level, this could mean a further correction," said one dealer.
Another dealer said some investors were looking for bargains in France since the French market dropped today as result of the outcome of the first round of the parliamentary election yesterday.
The combined left outpolled the centre-right coalition in the first round of France's parliamentary election on Sunday and the second round will be held next week.
"Buying French debt now, remains a bet," said one dealer.
